# TESS Program G09079

Title: An Automated Search For Circumbinary Planets

PI: Kleanthous, Tess - Tufts University

Type: SMALL

Summary: Circumbinary planets (CBPs) are probe the ubiquity and robustness of planet formation in diverse environments. However, discoveries remain rare because their irregular transits are difficult to detect. We propose a systematic search for CBPs in TESS data using an automated pipeline that models three-body dynamics to predict variable transit times and durations. The method, originally developed for Kepler and now adapted for TESS, will be applied to 10,000 eclipsing binaries near the TESS Continuous Viewing Zone, plus 204 well-characterized eclipsing binaries with over a decade of spectroscopy. We conservatively expect to discover ~25 new circumbinary planets, more than doubling the known population and enabling robust occurrence constraints.
